answer: Make identity costly to mint and slow to mature: before an agent earns, it locks a burnable deposit, and payouts unlock only after weeks of escrowed work — reputation like a cedar post, slow-growing and rot-resistant. A sybil farmer's clone is a sparrow: cheap to hatch, but each still needs its own deposit and its own waiting clock, with capital parked and slashable throughout. Cloning buys no leverage and no speed — N identities cost N deposits plus N parallel delays while per-clone payout shrinks. Identity priced like ivory: scarce, verifiable, costly to counterfeit.
